about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: 12 debt payoff cases worked to the cent
tasks.why: Midas is getting a payoff planner (avalanche, snowball and Joseph's own order). Claude checks its engine against cases worked by someone else. No real balances: every case is made up.
steps: Make 12 made-up cases: 4 avalanche, 4 snowball, 4 'custom order'. Each has 2 to 6 debts (name, balance, APR %, minimum payment) and one monthly budget at least the sum of the minimums.

Rules, exactly: each month, interest = balance x APR / 12 / 100, rounded to the cent (half up); add it to the balance; pay every minimum (or the whole balance if smaller); the rest of the budget goes to the target debt (avalanche = highest APR, snowball = lowest balance, custom = the order you list); if the target is paid off with money left, the rest goes to the next target the same month; when a debt hits 0 its minimum joins the rest from the next month.
Work every case month by month until every balance is 0.
At least 3 cases must run longer than 36 months and at least 2 must have a debt paid off in the same month another target changes.
tasks.done_when: 12 cases, every month listed, and Claude's engine gets the same balance for every debt in every month.
checks: Claude runs all 12 cases through its own engine; a balance more than $0.01 off in any month makes that case wrong.
Claude checks the 36-month and same-month conditions.
rejected_if: a case whose months stop before every balance is 0
a month that does not follow the rules above
fewer than 12 cases

tasks.title: 20 research findings on what really helps people pay off debt, each with its DOI
tasks.why: Joseph: the app must inspire him to get out of debt. Claude designs from evidence, not slogans.
inputs: Google Scholar, journal pages, NBER, Federal Reserve, CFPB (no blogs, no listicles, no AI summaries)
steps: Find 20 different published studies or official reports about paying down debt, motivation, small wins, framing, mental accounting, or progress feedback.

For each: full citation, DOI or official URL, the one finding in one sentence with its number (effect size, percent or dollars), and one concrete thing Midas should show because of it (a screen element, not advice).
Quote the abstract sentence the finding comes from, word for word.

deliver.shape: [{"n":1,"citation":"Gal, D. & McShane, B. (2012) ...","doi":"10....","finding":"...","quote":"exact sentence from the abstract","midas":"show ..."}] (20 objects)

tasks.done_when: 20 real studies, every DOI resolves to that paper, every quote is in its abstract.
checks: Claude resolves all 20 DOIs and searches each quote in the abstract.
One invented paper or invented quote = the whole file is rejected.
rejected_if: any paper that does not exist
a quote that is not word for word
a blog or news article in place of a study

tasks.title: 15 money apps taken apart: 75 things that make people keep going
tasks.why: Midas looked 'neon' and uninspiring. Claude wants the specific moves the best apps use.
inputs: the apps' own sites, help centres, App Store pages and press kits
steps: Apps: YNAB, Monarch Money, Copilot Money, Rocket Money, Undebt.it, Debt Payoff Planner, EveryDollar, Simplifi, Empower, Lunch Money, Actual Budget, Goodbudget, Origin, PocketGuard, Tiller.
For each app, 5 specific things on its screens that make you want to keep paying down or keep checking in (example: 'debt-free date shown under the total and it moves when you add a payment').
Each row: app, the screen it is on, what it does, a URL where it can be seen (a screenshot page, help article or store listing), and how Midas could do it better.
tasks.done_when: 75 rows, 5 per app, every URL shows what the row says.
checks: Claude opens 15 URLs at random.
Rows that only praise ('beautiful design') do not count.
rejected_if: a row copied from another row with the names changed
a source URL that does not open or does not say what the row claims
fewer items than the count
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
two rows that say the same thing about one app

tasks.title: Minimum payment formulas of 25 US card issuers, quoted from their cardholder agreements
tasks.why: Midas's payoff engine (src/plan.js) keeps each minimum fixed; real minimums fall as the balance falls. The engine needs each issuer's real formula.
steps: Take the 25 largest US card issuers (Chase, American Express, Citi, Capital One, Bank of America, Discover, Synchrony, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, Barclays, Goldman Sachs/Apple Card, PNC, TD Bank, Navy Federal, USAA, Truist, Credit One, Comenity/Bread, Fifth Third, Citizens, Huntington, Regions, KeyBank, BMO, First National).

From each one's own cardholder agreement or pricing page, copy the minimum payment rule: the percent of balance, what is added (interest, fees, past due), the dollar floor, and when the whole balance is due instead.
Write the rule as a formula over balance B, interest I, fees F: e.g. max(35, 0.01*B + I + F), or B when B < 35.

deliver.shape: [{"n":1,"issuer":"...","product":"the card or card family the agreement covers","formula":"max(40, 0.01*B + I + F)","floor_usd":40,"pct_of_balance":1,"adds":["interest","fees"],"url":"https://...","quote":"..."}]

tasks.done_when: 25 issuers, each formula traceable to the quoted agreement text.
checks: Claude opens 10 agreements at random and recomputes the formula from the quote.
Claude runs each formula on B=5000, I=80, F=0 and on B=20.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a formula from a blog or a calculator site instead of the issuer's own agreement
anything about Joseph's own accounts, balances, mail, messages or trades (public facts only)

tasks.title: How 25 issuers compute interest: balance method, day count, compounding, grace
tasks.why: Midas computes balance x APR / 12. Real cards compound daily on an average daily balance; the gap matters on large balances.
steps: For the same 25 issuers as MID-GEM-04: from the agreement's 'How we calculate your balance / interest' section copy the balance method (e.g. average daily balance including new transactions), the daily periodic rate (APR/365 or /360), whether interest compounds daily, the grace period in days and the minimum interest charge.
tasks.done_when: 25 rows, every field quoted or marked null with the reason in quote.
checks: Claude opens 10 at random.
day_count must be 360 or 365; grace_days a whole number.

tasks.title: 20 promo-rate products: deferred interest or true 0 %, quoted
tasks.why: Midas shows promo rates but does not model them; a deferred-interest promo charges all the back interest if not paid off in time.
steps: Pick 20 products a US consumer meets: 10 store cards (Synchrony / Comenity / TD retail cards), 5 buy-now-pay-later (Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay, PayPal Pay Later, Zip), 5 balance-transfer cards.
From each product's own terms page: promo type (deferred interest or 0 % intro APR), promo length, what happens when it ends, the go-to APR, the fee.

tasks.title: 25 hardship programs: what each lender offers and how to ask
tasks.why: The way out of debt is faster with a lower APR. Many issuers have hardship or APR-reduction programs; Joseph should know what to ask for.
steps: For 25 lenders (the 25 issuers above; swap in Discover Personal Loans, SoFi, LendingClub, Upstart for any with no public page): the program name, what it offers (APR cut, fee waiver, fixed payment plan, months), who qualifies, the phone path or web page to ask, and what it does to the account (closed, frozen, reported).
Quote the issuer's own page; when only the CFPB or a state regulator documents it, cite that page.

deliver.shape: [{"n":1,"lender":"...","program":"...","offers":"APR lowered to 9.99 % for 12 months","qualifies":"...","how_to_ask":"call the number on the back of the card, ask for the hardship team","account_effect":"card frozen during the plan","url":"https://...","quote":"..."}]

checks: Claude opens 10 at random.

tasks.title: 12 daily-compounding interest cases worked to the cent
tasks.why: Before Midas switches to daily interest (MID-GEM-05), Claude needs cases worked by hand to test it against.
steps: Make 12 cases with balances between 500 and 25,000, APRs between 9.99 and 29.99, three 30-day cycles each, one payment per cycle on day 20 (amount of your choice), no new purchases.
Daily periodic rate = APR / 365 / 100; interest accrues on the day's balance and is added at the end of each cycle (state whether it compounds daily or monthly; do both for cases 1-3).
Write every cycle: start balance, sum of daily balances, average daily balance, interest (rounded half up to the cent), payment, end balance.
tasks.done_when: 12 cases x 3 cycles; Claude recomputes every number in Python.
checks: A cycle off by more than 1 cent = the case fails; 2 failing cases = the file is sent back.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
numbers copied from an online calculator without the cycle rows

tasks.title: Give every debt in the book its APR, minimum, due day, limit and promo end
tasks.why: The new Debt screen plans the way out: it needs, for every card and loan, the numbers the bank shows. Without them it can only show balances.
steps: For every card and loan in the private ledger, add: apr (percent), min_payment, due_day (1-31), credit_limit (cards), promo_apr and promo_end (YYYY-MM-DD) when there is one, as_of (the statement date you read them from).
Read them from the statements and alerts in Joseph's email or the lender's site, never from memory.
Rebuild and encrypt the book with publish.sh as you do now; the plaintext never goes to Drive, Discord or GitHub.

deliver.folder: jpavia10/midas-ledger, a branch grok/... and a pull request

tasks.done_when: On the Debt screen, no card or loan shows 'APR missing' or 'minimum missing'.
checks: Joseph opens the Debt screen; the app lists every debt missing a field.
test/book.test.mjs checks the shape of every debt.
rejected_if: a number guessed or carried over without an as_of date
plaintext balances anywhere outside the encrypted book

tasks.title: A fresh book every Monday by noon PT
tasks.why: A ledger more than a week old makes every number on the screen a guess.
steps: Every Monday by 12:00 PT: refresh the 4 Plaid accounts, update balances, holds, stale/past-due/need-you marks, rebuild and encrypt with publish.sh.
Add one log line saying what changed (counts only, no amounts).
tasks.done_when: The app's 'built' stamp is never older than 7 days.
checks: the app shows the build age; Claude checks the commit dates
rejected_if: a week missed

tasks.title: The words of the way out: 24 milestone lines and 12 screen lines
tasks.why: When a card hits zero or the debt-free date moves closer, Midas says so. The lines must be plain and true, never cheesy.
steps: 24 milestone lines, one per event: first payment logged; each of 5%, 10%, 25%, 33%, 50%, 66%, 75%, 90%, 100% of starting debt paid; first card paid off; each further card paid off; debt-free date moves 1 month closer; 3, 6, 12 months in a row on plan; a month over plan; a month under plan (kind, no guilt); a new debt added (no guilt, a plan).
Each at most 90 characters, no exclamation marks, no emoji, uses {amount}, {months}, {name} where a number belongs (never a made-up number).
12 screen lines: one plain sentence under each main number on Home, Debt and Flow saying what it means.

deliver.shape: two tables: event | line ; number | line

checks: Claude counts characters and placeholders.
rejected_if: a line over 90 characters
a number that is not a placeholder
'journey', 'crush', 'smash', 'unlock'
